datasets.title: Raw data for AA7050 Specimen 01 - Relationships between microstructure and micromechanical stresses on local pitting
datasets.citation: Nicolas, Andrea; Da Silva Mello, Alberto; Sangid, Michael; https://doi.org/10.17632/hhf5sfk5bj.1
limitations: The provider describes one AA7050 specimen and one 300 by 400 micrometre region after two and six days; spatial pixels are repeated locations within one specimen, not independent specimens.
Dataset-level CC BY 4.0 permits reuse with attribution, license link and change notice; raw MAT files remain outside public source distributions while structure and embedded provenance are reviewed.

Matching filenames and a shared cropped region do not by themselves establish identical array coordinates, registration accuracy, height sign, length units, missing-value semantics or a state-label threshold.

Two exposure times from one specimen cannot identify a general Markov transition law, action effect, field corrosion rate, uncertainty distribution, probability of detection, remaining life or structural acceptance.
Stress and strain fields are same-study covariates, not independent corrosion truth; their coordinate frames and derivation must be reviewed before joining to morphology.

The related Corrosion Science article (DOI 10.1016/j.corsci.2019.03.016) describes AA7050-T7451 transverse-short specimens and states that local stresses were inferred with crystal-plasticity modelling; stress arrays are therefore model-derived fields rather than directly measured independent truth.

datasets.title: EBSD datasets for low-alloy steel weld metals - Arc, Laser, and Laser-hybrid welding
datasets.citation: Pauli Lehto (2021), https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5054204
limitations: The provider describes three EBSD map pairs for conventional arc, laser-hybrid and laser welds; exact physical specimen count, map areas, phase label schema and measurement uncertainty require archive-level audit.
EBSD pixels are spatially correlated measurements within a small number of weld specimens and are not independent coupons or qualification replicates.
The dataset license allows attributed reuse but does not qualify any phase threshold, material property, weld procedure, corrosion response or service-life inference.
The original ZIP remains in the excluded data/raw tree. Public redistribution of source point maps or derived pointwise observations requires a separate scope and attribution review.

datasets.title: AquaSolDB v2.1 gas solubility in water and brine compilation
datasets.citation: Abd, A.; Abushaikha, A. (2026), AquaSolDB v2.1; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23470595
datasets.license: CC-BY-4.0 for the compilation only; source measurements are not licensed by the compiler and require citation to the original paper
limitations: The v2.1 release contains compiled gas-solubility measurements from 499 cited sources; the compiler license covers the compilation, not the measurements in the cited papers.

Retain the version DOI, compiler attribution and transformation notes for any compilation-level reuse; any selected measurement requires its source_id paper citation and a separate rights/applicability review.

Only CO2 rows are candidates for this project, and only where solvent, salinity, temperature, pressure basis, gas composition, measurement status and flags support the intended thermodynamic interpretation.
Do not infer Henry coefficients from a finite-pressure solubility row without an explicitly reviewed thermodynamic conversion and fugacity basis.

The acquired archive is private research material in data/raw and excluded from packages; no row values, source references, headers copied from the provider, or pointwise derived values are redistributed.
The provider describes sampled checks of digitized values, not row-by-row verification; flagged, calculated, replicate, suspect and no-value records must remain distinguishable.

datasets.title: Harmonised first-year atmospheric corrosion database for carbon steel with ERA5 covariates
datasets.citation: Nguyen, Tien Thuy; https://doi.org/10.17632/ysr7wy3y7z.1
limitations: The package harmonises 617 programme records and 106 literature records; repeated sites, programmes and publications are not independent physical specimens.

Reported exposure observations originate in the cited programmes and publications. The dataset-level CC BY 4.0 declaration is kept separate from source-specific observation attribution and redistribution review.

ERA5/Open-Meteo weather covariates are recomputed model products rather than simultaneous specimen-level measurements, and must remain distinct from reported corrosion, chloride and sulfur-dioxide observations.

The provider validation tiers and pooled files must be preserved. Programme rows must not cross a source-group calibration/validation split, and provider scripts or fitted values are not independent observations.

First-year atmospheric carbon-steel loss does not qualify internal wet-CO2 corrosion, long-term power-law growth, localized penetration, structural capacity, remaining life or period failure probability.
Raw and pointwise derived observations remain outside public distributions; the public project records attribution, hashes, schema findings and aggregate inspection only.

datasets.title: Dataset for "Exploring Mechanism of Corrosion Inhibition of WE43 and AZ31 Alloys by Aqueous Molybdate in Hank's Solution by Multisine Impedimetric Monitoring"
datasets.citation: Kharytonau, Dzmitry; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10482561
limitations: Zenodo v1 declares CC0-1.0 for the deposited archive; preserve record DOI and dataset-level license metadata.
The archive contains raw microscopy, XPS and impedance files from the associated study; interpretation and specimen independence must follow deposited metadata, not inferred filenames.
Keep the downloaded archive in ignored local data/raw; do not copy pointwise records, images or derived values into package fixtures without their source lineage.
This EIS archive is experimental evidence for its declared alloy/electrolyte setup only; it does not establish field corrosion rates, generalized alloy ranking, acceptance or qualification.

datasets.title: Simulation and laboratory eddy current testing data - modelling compound defects via perturbation theory
datasets.citation: Friedrich, Alexander; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14186333
limitations: Simulation CSV and laboratory DICONDE are distinct evidence roles and must not be merged as independent physical specimens.
The laboratory DICONDE first pixel frame is provider-described as the real signal component and the second as the imaginary component; file-level tags and coordinate conventions require audit.
Commercial Faraday BEM simulation outputs do not grant redistribution or implementation rights for the solver itself.
Compound-defect fitting and same-study laboratory comparison are not general POD, crack sizing, material transfer or procedure qualification.

datasets.title: Datasets for Service-Like Creep-Fatigue Experiments on Grade P92 Steel
datasets.citation: Sonntag, Nadja; Jürgens, Maria; Uhlemann, Patrick; Skrotzki, Birgit; Olbricht, Jürgen; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7198219
limitations: Three service-like laboratory tests at 620 degC and declared low strain amplitude; transfer to other materials or temperatures is unqualified.
Waveform dwell and control modes must remain explicit; separate linear damage laws do not validate their interaction.

datasets.title: NCOMMS-23-27903B data
datasets.citation: Chen, Yi-Sheng; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10416768
limitations: Primary carbide-containing steel trapping, desorption, permeation and microscopy study; electrochemical charging is not gaseous-hydrogen fatigue-crack growth.

Main methods specify finite cylindrical TDS specimens and mass-ppm content in the article. Permeation membrane dimensions/area/potential reference and raw-to-article exposure-label correspondence require review. Planar transport verification is not a direct calibration to this TDS dataset.
The complete archive is about 2.64 GB. Fetch explicitly with --include-optional; raw files remain excluded from public distributions.
Local-equilibrium partition, kinetic desorption and fracture resistance are distinct models; do not infer one from another without geometry, boundary and mechanism evidence.

datasets.title: Experiment to measure the thickness loss due to corrosion of a 5mm uncoated steel sample exposed close to the shore during 6 months
datasets.citation: Cortés, Ainhoa; Irizar, Andoni; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13897090
limitations: One nominally 5 mm uncoated steel sample at one near-shore location was monitored for about six months; repeated measurements are not independent physical specimens, sites or fleet observations.

The provider describes two thickness measurements per day from an attached ultrasound sensor node. File-level clocks, raw waveforms, device settings, quality flags and reported thickness fields require inspection before any time-series model is fitted.

Sensor-reported thickness is not automatically destructive dimensional ground truth. Measurement uncertainty, calibration, spatial sampling footprint and any independent end-point thickness measurement must remain unresolved unless explicitly supplied by the source.
The provider-reported 134 micrometres per year is a dataset summary, not a bundled acceptance limit, transferable corrosion-rate prior, remaining-life estimate or failure probability.
Raw JSON observations remain outside public source distributions; public artifacts may contain attribution, checksums, independently authored readers and aggregate validation only.

datasets.title: Dataset of Charpy V-notch impact test records of nuclear structural materials
datasets.citation: Lee, Merickel, Kasala, Xu, Tang, Rittenhouse, Vakanski, Song (2025); https://doi.org/10.24435/materialscloud:p6-5y
limitations: Literature compilation: retain individual references and review source-specific rights before redistributing observations. Raw and normalized records are excluded from public packages.
Sub-sized and full-sized, irradiated and unirradiated specimens must not be pooled without a validated transformation.
Absorbed impact energy does not directly provide structural fracture toughness or an allowable operating temperature.

datasets.title: BAM Reference Data: Creep of Single-Crystal Ni-Based Superalloy CMSX-6
datasets.citation: Ávila Calderón, Luis A.; Schriever, Sina; Han, Ying; Olbricht, Juergen; Dolabella Portella, Pedro; Skrotzki, Birgit; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14750432
limitations: Twelve primary constant-load tests of one single-crystal alloy/orientation at one temperature; not a multi-temperature or multi-heat qualification set.
Preserve reported endpoint, specimen identity, initial nominal stress and data-reduction conventions. Do not infer thermal activation energy from one test temperature.
Data licensing and provenance are retained; raw observations and source document text are excluded from public distributions.

datasets.title: Dataset for publication "From surface preparation to cell operation: Reliable protective coatings for steel bipolar plates in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis"
datasets.citation: Egorov, Konstantin; Prestat, Michel; Blachier, Evan; Bhowmick, Sourav; Ringot, Geoffrey; Vucko, Flavien; Gupta, Abhay; Xu, Feina; Battaglia, Corsin; Maranzana, Gael; Heinz, Meike; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21390243
limitations: Steel bipolar plates in water electrolysis; assess transfer to pressure equipment separately.
Initial acquisition selects two small archives; remaining assets are catalogued but not acquired by default.

datasets.title: Recollected burst tests of experimental and FEM corroded pipelines.
datasets.citation: Amaya-Gomez; Munoz Giraldo; Schoefs; Bastidas-Arteaga; Sanchez-Silva; https://doi.org/10.17632/77t4k43y7g.1
limitations: Literature compilation: preserve experimental versus FEM records and original-reference groups; do not count simulations as independent physical tests.
Original source independence, diameter convention, missing mechanics and units must be checked against the acquired workbook before calibration.

The publisher page for Ma et al. (DOI 10.1016/j.engfailanal.2013.03.015) reports 79 collected full-scale tests. The compilation has 79 experimental rows with direct legend references plus 23 rows labelled Ma13Otros; that arithmetic does not resolve the latter rows' underlying publications, duplicates, specimens, or rights.
The documented metadata API returned HTTP 401, but the ordinary public page exposes a downloadable ZIP and SHA-256. The public UI route was verified and is used for acquisition.
Compilation CC0 is not treated as clearance of every original contribution. Raw and pointwise transformed observations are excluded from redistribution pending source-specific review.

datasets.title: COQTEL dataset: Corrosion Quantification Through Extended use of Lamb waves
datasets.citation: NICARD, Cyril; REBILLAT, Marc; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14193336
limitations: The two HDF5 files correspond to controlled experiments on separate nominally similar 1.5 mm 316L plates; repeated State_n groups within one file are time observations of one physical specimen, not independent specimens or fleet statistics.

The files pair electrochemical time, applied potential and current with 200 kHz Lamb-wave acquisitions. Electric charge, current and waveform change are not themselves measured pit radius, depth, wall loss, corrosion rate, remaining life or failure probability.

Each file has one root image without a state link or dimensional calibration. The article reports optical photographs at selected charge stages, but the HDF5 files do not provide pointwise pit dimensions for every state; do not treat the image as state-resolved ground truth.

Experiment 2 contains a reported air-bubble disturbance from states 30 through 100. Preserve that interval as an experimental anomaly rather than smoothing, deleting or interpreting it as corrosion damage.

The EC clocks are nondecreasing and contain 10 repeated terminal intervals in experiment 1 and 2 repeated intervals in experiment 2. Preserve same-time observations and never invent spacing from the nominal ten-second acquisition cycle.

Raw waveforms, electrochemical series, images and pointwise derived observations remain outside public source distributions; public artifacts contain attribution, checksums, independently authored readers and aggregate validation only.

datasets.title: Electrochemical Metrics for Corrosion Resistant Alloys
datasets.citation: Nyby et al.; https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.13038257.v2
limitations: The workbook compiles corrosion metrics reported across 81 publications; a row is not automatically an independently identified specimen or a directly reproduced primary measurement.
The Figshare workbook is CC BY 4.0, but that compilation license is not treated as proof that every underlying publication permits redistribution of its pointwise observations.

Pitting, repassivation and crevice potentials, critical temperatures, corrosion current and corrosion rate have different endpoints and test conditions and must not be merged into one ordinal resistance score without an explicit user model.
Material names, reference electrodes, environments, temperatures, scan protocols, censoring and duplicate literature observations require row-level inspection before fitting or validation.

datasets.title: Raw test data of C1 and C2 crack arrest toughness test
datasets.citation: Gao, Puyi; https://doi.org/10.17632/g69875w65c.1
limitations: The package reports C1 and C2 crack-arrest tests on ferritic/martensitic steel over 23 to -123 degrees Celsius; test validity, specimen identity and temperature must be preserved.
Crack-arrest toughness is not automatically an initiation toughness, service lower bound, FAD curve, crack-growth rate or failure probability.
Any workbook formulas, macros or provider analysis are treated as source content and are not executed. Raw and pointwise observations remain outside public distributions.
The first acquisition records a project SHA-256 because no publisher checksum was exposed on the public record page; later provider revisions require a new pinned catalog entry.

datasets.title: Dataset for: Cross-country Pipeline Inspection Data Analysis and Testing of Probabilistic Degradation Models
datasets.citation: Yarveisy, Rioshar; Khan, Faisal; Abbassi, Rouzbeh; https://doi.org/10.17632/c2h2jf5c54.1
limitations: The record describes four consecutive ILI datasets over more than seven years and more than 200 km, but public metadata does not establish raw MFL flux channels, sensor calibration, lift-off, velocity or magnetic-state records.
Inspection-year anomaly rows and third-party matching outputs are not independent physical specimens, excavation truth or qualified feature tracks.
A reviewed MIT repository contains processed parquet/CSV derivatives, but repository licensing is not treated as additional clearance or technical qualification of the underlying observations.

No pointwise data are bundled; the four provider-checksummed XLSX files are optional local research inputs and require field definitions and physical-identity review before any calibration/holdout design.

datasets.title: Data and code from: Multiscale fatigue crack initiation in hierarchical additively manufactured alloys
datasets.citation: Capaldi, Luc; Ford, Jamie; Fulco, Sage; Rai, Rajeev; Yang, Wuxian; Ching, Stephen; Stach, Eric; Turner, Kevin; Chen, Wen; Tertuliano, Ottman (2026); https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.vq83bk48n
datasets.license: CC0-1.0 per Dryad dataset policy and dataset API metadata
limitations: The provider README identifies processed macroscale AM single-edge-notched-beam fatigue outputs with cycle, delta-K in MPa*sqrt(m), crack extension in mm, and da/dN in m/cycle; it reports three physical specimens and R=0.1 at approximately 0.4 Hz.

The provider also supplies raw load/displacement/time histories and processed microscale J-based results. The present FCGR curve API applies only to an explicitly reviewed delta-K series; J-based microscale observations require a different driving-force contract.
The macroscale growth rates were derived from smoothed crack-length measurements using an incremental-polynomial procedure. They are processed observations, not raw independent growth measurements.
Do not treat repeated rows or specimens from the single study as independent publications or as steel, corrosion-fatigue, or general service validation.

Dryad API metadata provides the exact file digest and size, but the documented anonymous file download returned HTTP 401 in this environment. The archive was not acquired or inspected; catalog status remains metadata-only.

datasets.title: Dataset for: "Application of the Effective Critical Plane approach for the fatigue assessment of ductile cast iron under multiaxial and non-proportional loading conditions"
datasets.citation: Chiocca, Andrea; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14198237
limitations: Processed ECP factors and predictions share the study calibration workflow and are not independent validation targets for that method.
Row-level physical specimen identity, censoring and failure-endpoint definitions require article or protocol review before model fitting.
Underlying finite-element fields and meshes are not included; nominal stresses must not be treated as qualified notch-root histories.

datasets.title: Replication data for estimating below-ground natural-gas leak rate from above-ground measurements (ESCAPE-1)
datasets.citation: Cheptonui et al.; https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.8931zcrwq
limitations: The provider README states 5, 10, and 20 standard litres per minute but does not define the reference pressure and temperature needed for an SI molar-flow conversion.
Raw workbook time windows are not labelled as background, controlled-release steady state, transit, or recovery intervals.
The eleven experiment files share one campaign; physical and meteorological independence across files is unresolved.
Path-integrated methane response is not a calibrated leak-rate inversion, detection probability, field acceptance result, or FTA probability.

datasets.title: CT110 coiled-tubing weld and base-metal weight-loss corrosion rates
datasets.citation: Liu et al. (2021), https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0244237; supplements https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0244237.s017 and https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0244237.s018
limitations: The public fixture contains six values pairs transcribed from two CC BY 4.0 supplements and converted from mm/year to m/s; attribution and transformation are recorded in the fixture.
The observations come from one study and one reported CT110 product; physical coupon identities, replicate counts and rate uncertainty are not supplied in the supplements.
These points are a material contrast example, not a general wet-CO2 mechanistic calibration, transferable weld multiplier, acceptance result, life estimate or probability.
The original XLSX supplements are retained only under local data/raw and excluded from distributions; only the small attributed fixture is distributed.

datasets.title: The FABEST database: A benchmark fatigue dataset on 42CrMo4 +QT steel
datasets.citation: Papuga, Jan; Matusu, Martin; Pejkowski, Łukasz; Čapek, Jiří; Fojtik, Frantisek; Nesládek, Martin; Janssens, Koenraad; Muniz-Calvente, Miguel; Díaz Salamanca, Diego; Karolczuk, Aleksander; Trefil, Antonín; Mara, Vladimir; Halama, Radim; Kořínek, Michal; Tezel, Tugce; Swacha, Piotr; Křepela, Jan; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21509581
limitations: Inspect material heat, specimen, loading and censoring definitions before fitting; a benchmark compilation does not imply universal transfer.

Provider finish/interruption and the separate break-cycle field are preserved. All 60 high-cycle curve sheets omit the END criterion, so interruption is not automatically a runout and a break-cycle cell is not independent fracture confirmation.
Letter suffixes have unresolved specimen semantics. Free-text damage and temperature tags are screening aids, not retest, validity, self-heating or physical-specimen-independence decisions.
Macro-enabled workbook is parsed as data only; no embedded macros are executed or redistributed in the package.

datasets.title: FABEST High-Cycle Fatigue Competition: Participant Package for Blind Fatigue-Life Prediction
datasets.citation: Chiocca, Andrea; Papuga, Jan; Gkantou, Michaela; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23532147
limitations: The public release withholds blind target fatigue lives; loading definitions and calibration material do not constitute independent outcome validation.
Keep this competition package separate from the historical FABEST workbook; matching material names or specimen labels do not establish shared physical specimens.
Combined axial, torsional and internal-pressure challenge conditions require their own geometry, control, temperature and endpoint review before calibration or component transfer.

datasets.title: FABEST LCF Benchmark Dataset: Cyclic Softening, Ratcheting and Mean Stress Relaxation of 42CrMo4+QT Steel
datasets.citation: Halama, Radim; Kourousis, Kyriakos; Karamanos, Spyros A.; Papatheocharis, Theocharis; Kořínek, Michal; Natarajan, Ajay Vignesh; Pejkowski, Łukasz; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21420213
limitations: The fixed v2 archive contains 24 calibration experiment folders in Cases 1-3 and no CSV outcomes in the Cases 4-5 validation-target folder.
Archive experiment folders are retained as experiment identities; they do not independently declare physical specimen identities or prove specimen independence.

Four CSV roles per calibration experiment are kept distinct: ordered history, cycle summary, representative-cycle history and experiment summary. Rows and cycles are not counted as physical specimens.
Seven header families occur across the 96 calibration tables, including corrected and legacy naming variants. Callers must use the reviewed table header rather than positional guesses.
Raw archives, provider reports, submission templates and pointwise rows remain outside public distributions. Provider files and embedded templates are not executed.
Archive structure, row counts and benchmark scores do not validate a constitutive law, fatigue criterion, blind prediction, component transfer, remaining life, acceptance or failure probability.

datasets.title: Data for: Quantitative comparison of the predictions of fracture toughness temperature dependence by ASTM E1921 master curve and stress distribution T-scaling methods
datasets.citation: Meshii, Toshiyuki; Ishihara, Kenichi; Takagishi, Yoichi; Yakushi, Goh; Fujimoto, Yohei; https://doi.org/10.17632/2vkgrbsy8j.1
limitations: The workbook contains 448 training rows and 192 test rows from a paper-specific comparison; these labels are preserved as provider partitions rather than physical independence claims.

The temperature column is labeled K but includes negative values. The associated article identifies the tested-temperature feature and material ranges in degrees Celsius, which is recorded as the default reviewed interpretation while preserving the conflicting workbook label.

W, B and a have no adjacent workbook unit label. The associated article defines these dimensions and T-size thicknesses in millimetres, and all workbook thicknesses match that scale. Default ingestion records article_mm; callers can disable or override the review for derivative workbooks.

Material, specimen type and reviewed W/B form 34 source-specific geometry condition groups at the default 3 percent or 0.1 mm tolerance. Every group crosses the provider partition, so these strata expose split leakage and do not establish physical-specimen independence.

The associated article table provides article-local material/reference groups, not row-level literature identifiers. Exact, probable-name-variant, material-condition-mismatch and unresolved mappings remain distinct.

Seven of nine article-local references have resolved DOIs, but publication access or license metadata does not establish rights to redistribute the compiled observations. All 640 observation-rights states remain unresolved.
A dataset-level CC BY 4.0 declaration does not establish that every compiled underlying observation may be redistributed without source-specific review.
Do not treat training and testing labels, repeated temperatures or literature rows as independent specimens until identifiers and source relationships are checked.
Do not execute workbook formulas or macros. Raw and pointwise transformed observations remain outside public distributions.

datasets.title: Low carbon steel formed by DRECE method with hot dip zinc galvanizing and potentiodynamic polarization tests to study its corrosion behavior
datasets.citation: Vontorová, Jiřina; Novák, Vlastimil; Váňová, Petra; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13886478
limitations: Zinc-coated DRECE-processed steel and acid/salt laboratory polarization; not pressure-equipment field corrosion rates.
Tafel windows and solution-resistance treatment need an explicit procedure; no automatic extrapolation chosen from full curves.

datasets.title: Ultrasonic guided waves data for structural health monitoring of pipelines
datasets.citation: El Mountassir, Mahjoub; https://doi.org/10.17632/ttb63krg6d.1
limitations: One laboratory steel tube was monitored under approximately 19 to 26 degrees Celsius; repeated acquisitions are not independent physical specimens or fleet observations.
The first 207 reported signals represent the healthy period and 29 signals follow six sequentially machined corrosion-like damage steps; machining steps are not natural corrosion time evolution.
The raw guided-wave amplitudes are not direct remaining-wall-thickness measurements and must not be supplied to the Bayesian thickness update without a separately calibrated observation model.

Five excitation frequencies, torsional and flexural modes, five repeated acquisitions and the provider DAC column have distinct roles; DAC is provider processing content rather than an observed damage channel.
Damage dimensions by step, timestamp mapping, temperature identity and acquisition-to-step grouping require file-level inspection before detection or sizing validation.

datasets.title: Research Data on Fatigue Tests of As-Welded, Deep-Rolled, and HFMI-Treated Joints
datasets.citation: Christian Daenekas; Leibniz University Hannover; 10.25835/0dojws6u
limitations: Repeated specimen identifiers include interrupted or repeated loading stages.
Runouts are right-censored observations, not failures.
Separate material, stress ratio and treatment; split by specimen to avoid leakage.

datasets.title: HE-Austenite: Hydrogen Embrittlement of Austenitic Stainless Steels in Gaseous Hydrogen, Separating Weld Metal from Base metal, with Per-Heat Composition
datasets.citation: Faizan, Muhammad; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23107780
limitations: Literature compilation of gaseous-hydrogen tests, not a new primary experiment. Retain source, material heat, weld zone, reference environment and extraction provenance.
Provider CC BY 4.0 does not clear all underlying literature; raw and pointwise transformed observations remain excluded from public distributions.
Tensile retention, fatigue life and crack-growth outcomes are different observables. Do not convert electrochemical charging to an equivalent gas pressure or a property ratio to failure probability.
Fixed deposit contains internal snapshot differences: 15 CSV versus linked-composition discrepancies. Preserve both values; plastic-strain units and pressure conventions remain unresolved.

datasets.title: Heterogenous CO2 Corrosion Dataset
datasets.citation: Ejeta, Joan; North Carolina A&T State University; https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/1ZIEO4
limitations: The provider describes a heterogeneous compilation of field, simulated and literature experimental data; data type, source identity and observation hierarchy must be audited before model fitting.
The dataset-level CC0 declaration is kept separate from attribution, transformation and redistribution review for observations drawn from underlying literature.
Rows must not be treated as independent physical specimens unless the source supplies that identity.

The CSV omits units. The associated CC BY 4.0 preprint at doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-8896642/v1 supplies a reviewed column-unit basis, but water chemistry, exposure duration, material condition and row-level source mapping remain unresolved.

The paper reports aggregate composition of 243 NORSOK M-506-generated, 50 autoclave weight-loss, 60 eastern-Hainan field and 74 Egua-2 field observations; it does not map those groups to CSV row numbers.

A caller-held accepted manuscript cited for the autoclave source contains 22 rows, not the reported 50. One unique 22-row temperature/velocity/pH/rate sequence candidate occurs at provider rows 334-355, but three MPa-to-bar pressure comparisons disagree; this remains candidate evidence rather than a qualified source-group assignment.

An official 2025 secondary article reproduces eastern-Hainan primary rows 1-4 and 60. Six transformed non-response fields uniquely match compilation provider rows 245-248 and 304; the first four reproduced corrosion rates match, while reproduced row 60 reports 3.11 mm/year against 2.86 in the compilation. The unreproduced 55 rows and the group assignment remain unqualified.

The official publisher preview for the Egua-2 article is only twelve pages: the target appears in the contents, but the included body begins a different article and exposes none of the Egua-2 observation tables. It supplies no row-level evidence for the reported 74 observations.
No row may be promoted to a wet-CO2 mechanistic calibration target, structural acceptance value, remaining life or failure probability solely because it appears in the compilation.
Raw and pointwise derived observations remain outside public distributions until the row-level provenance and rights audit is complete.

datasets.title: Effect of Hydrogen Embrittlement on Mechanical Properties of Additively Manufactured 316L Stainless Steel
datasets.citation: Kresta, Michal; Konečná, Kateřina; Váňová, Petra; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19813205
limitations: Additively manufactured 316L with electrolytic charging; not gaseous-hydrogen pressure-vessel qualification.
Workbook specimen and processing conditions must accompany any fitted model.

datasets.title: RECORD-SAND2012-7321 4130X vessel Q&T
datasets.citation: Sandia National Laboratories; HyMatBase record j1e8n-2bz97; related work PVP2010-25827
limitations: The provider record exposes the workbook for download but its Rights section is blank; the workbook remains a local research input and is not redistributed.

The record identifies quenched-and-tempered 4130X pressure-vessel steel, a tempered-martensite condition, hydrogen at 25 degC and 4.5 MPa, and a 607 MPa reference-environment yield strength; row-level conditions must still be audited.
Spreadsheet plots, fitted lines and repeated source rows are not independent observations and must be separated from pointwise measurements.
Availability and a provider MD5 do not qualify test validity, fracture resistance, fatigue life, component transfer or a design curve.

datasets.title: Aqueous electrolytes (Otto robotic electrolyte study)
datasets.citation: Dave et al.; Cell Reports Physical Science 1 (2020) 100264; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrp.2020.100264; dataset https://data.matr.io/5/
limitations: The provider page lists otto_aqueous.json and otto_aqueous.pkl and declares CC BY 4.0 for the dataset. This project downloaded the provider ZIP to the excluded data/raw tree and reads only its JSON member.
The provider publishes no cryptographic checksum for the ZIP. The recorded archive and JSON SHA-256 values are locally observed snapshot pins, not publisher checksums.

The records are fixed-current electrolyte-stability measurements on platinum and associated pH/conductivity values. They are not corrosion-polarization scans, corrosion rates, metal-loss values, or corrosion-calibration records.
Conductivity and temperature numbers have no unit string in the JSON file; preserve them in provider-native units and do not convert until the relevant unit basis is independently reviewed.
The article describing the work has a separate CC BY-NC-ND notice. The dataset page declares CC BY 4.0 for the deposited dataset; do not copy article prose, figures or tables into project materials.
Attribution is required for any reuse; the local raw archive remains excluded from public package builds.

datasets.title: 304L chloride-induced SCC under atmospheric salt loading
datasets.citation: Scatigno, Dong, Ryan and Wenman (2019); https://doi.org/10.17632/mrwrphjvjr.1
limitations: The provider describes an Excel supplement with corrosion area, crack velocity and crack density for 304L stainless steel under chloride-containing atmospheric exposure.

The dataset page declares CC BY 4.0 and cites a peer-reviewed article. The repository archives the provider version and attribution metadata; this does not independently establish rights to any third-party item that may be embedded in the workbook.
